xsdmMle 0.1.0
  • Reference

    Compute log(1 ± exp(-a)) Accurately and Efficiently

    log1mexp.Rd

    This function computes \(\log(1 - \exp(-a))\) or \(\log(1 + \exp(x))\) in a numerically stable way, avoiding catastrophic cancellation for small or large values of a. The implementation is adapted from the copula package.

    log1mexp(a, cutoff = log(2))

    Arguments

    a

    numeric vector of non-negative values. NA values are allowed and preserved.

    cutoff

    numeric scalar, positive threshold used to decide which formula to apply. The default log(2) is near-optimal for numerical stability, but any value in [0.5, 1] works well.

    Value

    A numeric vector of the same length as a, where each element is:

    • \(\log(1 - \exp(-a))\) for positive a, computed accurately.

    • Preserves NA values from input.

    Details

    Direct computation of \(\log(1 - \exp(-a))\) can suffer from floating-point errors when a is small or large. This function switches between:

    • log(-expm1(-a)) when a <= cutoff, for better precision in small a.

    • log1p(-exp(-a)) when a > cutoff, for better precision in large a.

    Note

    If any a < 0, a warning is issued since the formula assumes a >= 0.

    See also

    log1p, expm1

    Examples

    # Compare different approaches for a range of values
a <- 2^seq(-58, 10, length = 256)
f_expr <- expression(
  log(1 - exp(-a)),
  log(-expm1(-a)),
  log1p(-exp(-a)),
  log1mexp(a)
)
names(f_expr) <- c("Direct", "expm1", "log1p", "Stable")
fa <- do.call(cbind, as.list(f_expr))
head(fa) # expm1() works well for small a
#>      Direct     expm1 log1p    Stable
#> [1,]   -Inf -40.20254  -Inf -40.20254
#> [2,]   -Inf -40.01770  -Inf -40.01770
#> [3,]   -Inf -39.83286  -Inf -39.83286
#> [4,]   -Inf -39.64802  -Inf -39.64802
#> [5,]   -Inf -39.46318  -Inf -39.46318
#> [6,]   -Inf -39.27834  -Inf -39.27834
tail(fa) # log1p() works well for large a
#>        Direct expm1          log1p         Stable
#> [251,]      0     0 -3.263800e-177 -3.263800e-177
#> [252,]      0     0 -4.814940e-213 -4.814940e-213
#> [253,]      0     0 -3.774342e-256 -3.774342e-256
#> [254,]      0     0 -5.242582e-308 -5.242582e-308
#> [255,]      0     0   0.000000e+00   0.000000e+00
#> [256,]      0     0   0.000000e+00   0.000000e+00
